The Program
 
Neurodivergent individuals will play a disproportionate role in shaping the future of America and the West. They see past performative ideologies and perceive beauty in the world that still exists — which technology and art can expose.
 
The current LLM tech landscape positions them to dominate. Pattern recognition. Non-linear thinking. Hyperfocus. The cognitive traits that make the neurodivergent different are precisely what make them exceptional in an AI-driven world.
 
Palantir is launching the Neurodivergent Fellowship as a recruitment pathway for exceptional neurodivergent talent. This is not a diversity initiative. We believe neurodivergent individuals will have a competitive advantage as elite builders of the next technological era, and we're hiring accordingly for all roles.
 
This program is designed for those who think differently, and that's the point. Whether you're self-taught, formally educated, or somewhere in between, we're looking for builders who can see patterns others miss and solutions others overlook.
 
The Role
 
You'll join Palantir as a full-time employee to build software and deliver customer outcomes. You'll work on real problems: helping customers deploy AI-powered solutions, building the software platforms of the future, and transforming how organizations operate. You'll be held to the same performance standards as any Palantir engineer, and your career progression will be based purely on merit and impact.
 
We move fast. We expect excellence. We don't require you to sit still.
 
What We’re Looking For
 
We want excellent people from any background (no formal diagnosis or disclosure required).

title: Backend Software Engineer - Infrastructure
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organizations use data. Our Software Engineers are involved throughout the product lifecycle, from idea generation, design, prototyping, and production delivery. You will collaborate closely with technical and non-technical teammates to understand our customers' problems and build products that solve them. We encourage movement across teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll learn about many different technologies and aspects of each product. Engineers work autonomously and make decisions independently, within a community that will support and challenge you as you grow and develop, becoming a strong technical contributor and engineering leader.
 
Our Product Development organization is made up of small teams of Software Engineers. Each team focuses on a specific aspect of a product. Our infrastructure teams are responsible for the lowest layers of our software stack, often focused on database technologies, distributed systems, large scale data systems, security, and application infrastructure. As a Software Engineer on infrastructure working on our Foundry platform, you'll contribute high-quality code to underpin Palantir Foundry and Gotham with performant, secure, and scalable building blocks, enabling products deployed to the most important institutions in the public and private sector. You'll build the foundational capabilities that power our products used by research scientists, aerospace engineers, intelligence analysts, and economic forecasters, in countries around the world.
 
We’re hiring engineers who are passionate about solving real-world problems and empowering both developers and end-users to work optimally. If you’re motivated to develop reliable, performant, and scalable systems, and to design robust APIs and primitives, this role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our products and the people who use them.
 
Frontline
 
Foundry Software Engineers may be offered the opportunity to Frontline, an exclusive program unlike any other. This unique, short-term assignment involves being embedded with customers, allowing you to work directly with users and gain firsthand insight into how our products are used and the challenges our customers face. Unlike traditional engineering roles, Frontline immerses you in complex, ambiguous problems, empowering you to deliver impactful solutions across some of the world’s most important industries and institutions.
 
Some of our most successful products were built on the factory floor, addressing real-world problems for the world's most important institutions. These products were developed by some of our most successful product engineers, who began their careers in roles aligned with Frontline responsibilities, gaining a deep understanding of both our technology and our customers.
 
Frontliners operate across a broad spectrum of responsibilities, much like a startup CTO. They work in small teams to own the end-to-end execution of high-stakes projects. This spectrum ranges from discussing architecture and building custom web apps to conducting workshops with users and strategizing with customer executives. No two days are alike, as each day is diverse and impactful. By witnessing how customers engage with Foundry and experiencing these pain points firsthand, you’ll gain unique insights that feed directly back into our development process, helping to refine and enhance our products.

title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer, New Grad - Commercial
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
The Forward Deployed Software Engineer 
 
Forward Deployed Engineering is a radical commitment to the outcome. This is Palantir’s operating ethos. We pioneered this unique position, embedding engineers directly with our customers to tackle their most pressing challenges head-on. As an FDE, you’ll be at the intersection of world-changing problems and impactful technology, shaping solutions where they matter most.

From hospital beds to factory floors, Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) embed themselves in the customer’s reality until the problem is theirs. This requires walking many miles in a customer’s shoes, building past the perimeter of what the product currently offers, and deviating from every pre-existing formula to solve the problem. Whether that problem is “How do we predict and mitigate wildfire risks across a power grid?” or “How can we analyze and adapt a global supply chain to deliver critical parts on time?” You’ll use your technical expertise, creativity, and problem-solving skills to drive real-world impact.
 
Core Responsibilities 
 
To solve mission-critical problems by deploying software and AI into the high stakes operations of the world’s leading institutions. This requires a ruthless commitment to truth-seeking and prioritizing real outcomes. 

The work is difficult. The stakes are real. You will work in small, high-trust teams and own projects end-to-end, from the first conversation with a customer, to shipping the product that changes how they operate. You will embed with the customer, the chaos, and the consequences, and will be entrusted with real ownership to:
Collaborate with engineers to make architecture and design decisions
Wrestle with data at a scale that breaks assumptions and demands invention
Build custom applications, LLM workflows, and production solutions engineered for a specific customer's reality
Own relationships with stakeholders from the users in the weeds to the executives making the calls
As a New Grad, you will be entrusted with responsibility on day 1. You will not be handed a ticket queue. You will not be shielded from the customer, the chaos, or the consequences. FDEs are entrusted with real ownership, operating with real autonomy, and held to a real standard, no matter their tenure.

title: Meritocracy Fellowship
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.
 
The Program
 
We believe meritocracy is the operating system for execution: find ability wherever it exists, give people room to act, and judge them by the quality of what they do.

The American university once advanced this vision extraordinarily well. At its best, it found talented individuals from every background, exposed them to challenging ideas, and sent them into the world sharper, more capable, and imbued with purpose. When it worked, it was extraordinary.

Yet in recent decades, many of our finest institutions strayed from this calling. Admissions committees elevated other priorities. Classrooms rewarded conformity over honesty and rigor. Credentials replaced true capability. Cost became decoupled from value.

We launched the Meritocracy Fellowship to recover that highest purpose: find exceptionally talented individuals, forge them intellectually, give them responsibility, and judge them by their achievements alone. Based purely on merit and academic excellence, graduating high school students will be invited to interview, and select applicants will receive a Meritocracy Fellowship. Those that excel will obtain offers to join Palantir full time.

Skip the debt. Get the real education. Earn the Palantir degree.
 
The Curriculum
 
For five weeks, Fellows grapple with the ideas that shape our civilization. What is the West? Is it worth defending? In what ways is America exceptional within this broader context? And what is Palantir's mission in that context?

Fellows read great works, visit institutions at the frontiers of knowledge and public life, and work alongside one another to build something real. This is the education that universities were designed to deliver: rigorous, Socratic, grounded in the texts and ideas that actually matter. Not a lecture hall. Not a curriculum designed by committee. A room full of people who are smarter than you, expecting you to hold your own.

This initial period lays the intellectual foundation before Fellows join forward-deployed engineering or internal software teams. Fellows spend substantial time building in the first five weeks and learn from Palantirians working across engineering, product, security, deployment, and operations.

Our most vital technologies cannot be created by those indifferent to their purpose. Today's challenges demand builders who are guided by conviction and a clear sense of mission.
 
The Role
 
Once Fellows join Palantir's development or forward deployed engineering teams, they are treated like any other Palantir software engineer: joining a team and working alongside customers onsite.

Fellows are not given internship projects; they are given the responsibility of a full-time engineer. They learn the problem from the people who live it, build against real data, ship software, and iterate. The data is real. The stakes are real. The people depending on the outcome are real.

In this role, the challenges you'll seek will require a curious and analytical approach, a sharp intuition for product, and a strong degree of user insight. You will be matched to roles based on your skills, interests, and experience.

The only factor that determines whether you advance here is outcomes.

description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
The Palantir Design Team is responsible for the human experience of using our software. Our team is growing rapidly, but we're committed to creating a tight-knit team environment that fosters trust, integrity, empathy, and growth. We work together in realizing a shared product vision, and regularly give feedback and critique to each other.
 
Designing at Palantir is a varied experience. On a given day, you might be: leading a design sprint for your product team; designing a micro-interaction to make a complex analytical task feel simple; and/or advocating for UX consistency by creating flexible, reusable UI components.
 
Core Responsibilities
 
• Interaction and visual design. As a product designer, you'll be involved at every stage of design work. You'll help define early product concepts, flesh out the high-level workflow and micro-interactions of a feature, and execute on a crisp and effective visual design. You should have experience with some of the following mockup and prototyping tools: Sketch, Framer, Principle, Figma, Invision.
• User research. We frequently do informal user research, and value people who can be flexible with research processes and methodologies to achieve the right outcome. You'll often visit customer offices to interview and learn from the users we serve. You'll pair qualitative methods (e.g. scripted usability tests and contextual inquiry) with quantitative information, like product and usage metrics.
• Prototyping. You will prototype—using software like Principle and Framer, or another favorite method—both to communicate your designs and validate your decisions.
• Partnering with engineers. We work closely with product and forward deployed engineers to realize our design ideas. You'll treat engineers as partners and collaborate with them to prototype and build out products.
• Awareness of how software interfaces are built. Familiarity with HTML, CSS, Javascript, and Typescript is appreciated. You don't need to be an expert—just fluent enough to collaborate with engineers, and know what's possible with frontend technologies. Resources and mentorship are available to designers who want to learn more.
 
Designers at Palantir have great autonomy over their work, so a wide skill set is necessary. However, many designers on the team are also passionate experts in one area. You might be the kind of designer who ships code every week, or the kind of designer who shares detailed user research findings with your team.

description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
Forward Deployed Engineering is a radical commitment to the outcome. This is Palantir’s operating ethos. We pioneered this unique position, embedding engineers directly with our customers to tackle their most pressing challenges head-on. As an FDE, you’ll be at the intersection of world-changing problems and impactful technology, shaping solutions where they matter most.

From hospital beds to factory floors, Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) embed themselves in the customer’s reality until the problem is theirs. This requires walking many miles in a customer’s shoes, building past the perimeter of what the product currently offers, and deviating from every pre-existing formula to solve the problem. Whether that problem is “How do we predict and mitigate wildfire risks across a power grid?” or “How can we analyze and adapt a global supply chain to deliver critical parts on time?”, you’ll use your technical expertise, creativity, and problem-solving skills to drive real-world impact.
 
Core Responsibilities
 
To solve mission-critical problems by deploying software and AI into the high stakes operations of the world’s leading institutions. This requires a ruthless commitment to truth-seeking and prioritizing real outcomes. 

The work is difficult. The stakes are real. You will work in small, high-trust teams and own projects end-to-end, from the first conversation with a customer, to shipping the product that changes how they operate. You will embed with the customer, the chaos, and the consequences, and will be entrusted with real ownership to: 
Collaborate with engineers to make architecture and design decisions
Wrestle with data at a scale that breaks assumptions and demands invention
Build custom applications, LLM workflows, and production solutions engineered for a specific customer's reality
Own relationships with stakeholders from the users in the weeds to the executives making the calls
 As an Intern, you will be entrusted with responsibility on day 1 and expected to learn quickly. You will not be handed a low-risk or unimportant project. You will not be shielded from the customer, the chaos, or the consequences. FDEs are entrusted with real ownership, operating with real autonomy, and held to a real standard, no matter their tenure.

title: Privacy and Civil Liberties Software Engineer, Internship
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
The Privacy and Civil Liberties (PCL) Engineering team is a interdisciplinary team of software engineers, forward-deployed engineers, designers, lawyers, and policy experts. The first of its kind in the tech industry, Palantir’s PCL team was formed 15+ years ago as a rejection of the prevailing view that privacy protections must be sacrificed to national security interest. Today, the mission of the PCL team goes far beyond civil liberties protections, and our work challenges other false tradeoffs between operational effectiveness and the defining values of our society: Effective military operations should not be at odds with protecting civilians and upholding the Law of Armed Conflict. Deploying AI with scale and speed should never compromise safety, reliability, and governance. The PCL team builds software and forward deploys to ensure that our customers can pursue their hardest operational challenges while keeping ethical imperatives in plain sight. You can read more about the team on the Palantir blog here.

As a PCL Engineer, you will be responsible for designing and developing full-stack software products for privacy, data protection, AI governance, and accountability in Palantir’s software platforms. You may build security and governance primitives in our platform, applications for auditors, user-facing workflows for AI governance, internal tools for data protection, or something new all-together to help our customers address their next set of challenges. In every case, the software that you build will directly help our customers both carry out their missions more effectively and better meet their legal and ethical obligations. As part of this role, your efforts will be informed by collaborations with technical and non-technical teammates to understand our customers’ key challenges. Your technical approaches will entail engaging with and even helping to shape the latest developments in law and policy. 

The skills and background of successful candidates may vary highly, but curiosity, grit, and a drive to run toward hard socio-technical problems are critical for our team. We’re looking for engineers who are passionate about addressing real-world challenges and empowering our customers to carry out their workflows both effectively and responsibly.

title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer, Internship - Commercial
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Forward Deployed Engineer, Internship
Forward Deployed Engineering is a radical commitment to the outcome. This is Palantir’s operating ethos. We pioneered this unique position, embedding engineers directly with our customers to tackle their most pressing challenges head-on. As an FDE, you’ll be at the intersection of world-changing problems and impactful technology, shaping solutions where they matter most.

From hospital beds to factory floors, Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) embed themselves in the customer’s reality until the problem is theirs. This requires walking many miles in a customer’s shoes, building past the perimeter of what the product currently offers, and deviating from every pre-existing formula to solve the problem. Whether that problem is “How do we predict and mitigate wildfire risks across a power grid?” or “How can we analyze and adapt a global supply chain to deliver critical parts on time?” You’ll use your technical expertise, creativity, and problem-solving skills to drive real-world impact.
 
Core Responsibilities 
 
To solve mission-critical problems by deploying software and AI into the high stakes operations of the world’s leading institutions. This requires a ruthless commitment to truth-seeking and prioritizing real outcomes. 

The work is difficult. The stakes are real. You will work in small, high-trust teams and own projects end-to-end, from the first conversation with a customer, to shipping the product that changes how they operate. You will embed with the customer, the chaos, and the consequences, and will be entrusted with real ownership to: 
Collaborate with engineers to make architecture and design decisions
Wrestle with data at a scale that breaks assumptions and demands invention
Build custom applications, LLM workflows, and production solutions engineered for a specific customer's reality
Own relationships with stakeholders from the users in the weeds to the executives making the calls
 As an Intern, you will be entrusted with responsibility on day 1. You will not be handed a ticket queue. You will not be shielded from the customer, the chaos, or the consequences. FDEs are entrusted with real ownership, operating with real autonomy, and held to a real standard, no matter their tenure.

title: Deployment Strategist
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


What We're About
 
At its core, this role is about uncovering dots and—without knowing the shape they form—figuring out how to connect them. Our customers come to us with a hunch that the only way to protect their troops, manufacture high-quality products, structure effective healthcare policies, or deliver aid to refugees safely is to make better use of their data. Deployment Strategists are responsible for turning that hunch into reality.
 
If you believe in the transformational power of data and technology and in your own ability to bring that power to bear against complex problems, we want to meet you.
 
What We Do
 
As a Deployment Strategist, you'll work as part of a driven and creative team of Engineers, Product Designers, and other Deployment Strategists to deploy software against the most challenging problems our world faces. Your mission is to synthesize disconnected streams of thought into a cohesive understanding of what the most important problem is, what the data means, what the product needs, what users are motivated by, and where the impact could be.
 
Deployment Strategists are do-ers who immerse themselves in our customers' most intricate workflows, partner with customer teams and explore the data, and dive into the product landscape to enable us to scale. A select number of Deployments Strategists may also be deployed to Palantir internal teams and problems. In this role, the problems you'll tackle will require a curious and analytical mindset, a sharp intuition for product, and a strong degree of user empathy to ultimately empower our customers to make better decisions.

title: Product Designer
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
The Palantir Design Team is responsible for the human experience of using our software. Our team is growing rapidly, but we're committed to creating a tight-knit team environment that fosters trust, integrity, empathy, and growth. We work together in realising a shared product vision, and regularly give feedback and critique to each other.
 
Designing at Palantir is a varied experience. On a given day, you might be: leading a design sprint for your product team; designing a micro-interaction to make a complex analytical task feel simple; and/or advocating for UX consistency by creating flexible, reusable UI components.
 
You consider things like API documentation, SDK functionality, and developer onboarding and can speak the language of a developer. You have familiarity with existing developer tooling and have strong understanding of developer workflows. 
 
Core Responsibilities
 
• Interaction and visual design. As a product designer, you'll be involved at every stage of design work. You'll help define early product concepts, flesh out the high-level workflow and micro-interactions of a feature, and execute on a crisp and effective visual design. You should have experience with mockup and prototyping tools.
• User research. We frequently do informal user research, and value people who can be flexible with research processes and methodologies to achieve the right outcome.
• Prototyping. You will prototype, both to communicate your designs and validate your decisions.
• Partnering with engineers. We work closely with product and forward deployed engineers to realize our design ideas. You'll treat engineers as partners and collaborate with them to prototype and build out products.
• Awareness of how software interfaces are built. Familiarity with HTML, CSS, Javascript, and Typescript is appreciated. You don't need to be an expert—just fluent enough to collaborate with engineers, and know what's possible with frontend technologies. Resources and mentorship are available to designers who want to learn more.
 
Designers at Palantir have great autonomy over their work, so a wide skill set is necessary. However, many designers on the team are also passionate experts in one area. You might be the kind of designer who ships code every week, or the kind of designer who shares detailed user research findings with your team.

title: Head of BD - NATO
description:
About us

At Viasat, the work you do helps people stay connected in ways that matter, from everyday moments to critical missions across air, land, sea, and space.

We’re a place for people who are curious, bold, and motivated by meaningful work. Here, you'll have the opportunity to make an impact, explore new possibilities, and grow your career in ways that align with your interests and goals. When you're ready to take on something new, you'll find leaders who support your development and help you turn your ambition into action.


What you'll do

The Key Markets Team is responsible for developing Viasat International Government's business in strategic growth markets. NATO is a fast growing market for Viasat with several campaigns being pursued in the Government sector.

This is a senior role that will cut across Viasat International Government and Viasat Government business. The candidate will be responsible for all business development activities that fall within NATO and be the key liaisons point for the business with NCIA and NSPA. They will be responsible for lead generation, opportunity development, campaign management with the business areas and stakeholder management with a focus on pipeline generation.

The candidate needs to have a good working knowledge of NATO setup, infrastructure and priorities as well as regional impact on NATO policy (Black Sea, High North, Eastern Flank, Baltics). A strong background in government sector business and the ability to work cross-domain, cross-functional and cross-business in virtual team set-ups is highly desirable.

The solutions that will be developed and delivered will allow government customers to deliver mission-critical communications and assure end users that they can operate with confidence to deliver outcomes, either as part of NATO programmes and/or capability procured by Member States through NATO frameworks.

The candidate will have the unique opportunity to work with business areas, business units, functional leaders and team members and corporate functions. Given the importance of the role there will be significant exposure with senior leadership.


The day-to-day

The day-to-day

What’s the day-to-day like for this candidate?

  • Defining and owning the strategy and deliverables that will enable business growth
  • Developing the long-term pipeline that will form part of the VIG long range business plan (LRBP)
  • Developing new business with support from the business areas
  • Collaborating across business functions to support NATO BD activity
  • Leading and managing stakeholder engagement
  • Leading NATO campaigns and captures with the business areas
  • Developing business cases to support NATO BD and market development activity that will increase Viasat Pwin and visibility
  • Working with strategic advisors

What you'll need

  • What you'll need

    • The ability to work with a diverse cross-business, cross-functional team
    • Self-motivated, passionate and confident to work in-region, often on their own with support from the business
    • Relevant experience in working with government sector with a preference of working with NATO (directly or as a supplier).
    • Defence prime/OEM experience essential (working with or for)
    • Satellite Communications and/or Space Sector experience.

What will help you on the job

  • What will help you on the job

    • Experience engaging in public forums and public speaking (voice of the business in NATO)
    • Solid understanding of satellite communications and space infrastructure use cases in government context
    • Ability to simplify complex solutions to enable stronger customer engagement at the solutions phase – articulate the benefits of our solutions in customer mission sets
    • Postgraduate degree in a technical, business or international relations discipline

EEO Statement

Viasat is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, seeking to create a welcoming and diverse environment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, marital status, genetics, age, or veteran status or any other applicable legally protected status or characteristic. If you would like to request an accommodation on the basis of disability for completing this on-line application, please click here.

title: Validation Engineer | Luma
description:
Our Why At Dotmatics

At Dotmatics, a Siemens company, we believe science, data, and decision-making must be deeply intertwined for innovation to thrive. Our Portfolio includes Luma, LumaLab Connect, ELN Platform, Graphpad Prism, Geneious, SnapGene, Protein Metrics, OMIQ, FCS Express, LabArchives, NQuery, EasyPanel, SoftGenetics and Virscidian.

We have a vision for a new Lab of the Future that will change the future of scientific research.

We have created the world’s most comprehensive digital science platform – best-of-breed software applications already used by more than 2 million scientists, together in a single ecosystem united by a powerful, flexible enterprise data platform. This is not flat data buried away in digital graveyards. This is dynamic, multi-dimensional decision-making.

Scientific enterprises need a new level of effectiveness to achieve tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Illness will not wait. The biosphere will not wait. We are tireless in our vision, because the time for innovation is now.

Shaping the Future of Science At Dotmatics

Our global team of more than 800 colleagues are dedicated to supporting our customers in over 180 countries. Together, with our scientific community of users, we accelerate scientific innovation in order to make the world a healthier, cleaner, and safer place to live.

You’ll join a collaborative, global team pushing the boundaries of scientific innovation. Your ideas and efforts will have a tangible impact, accelerating scientific progress and discovery. We offer a dynamic, remote-friendly environment that fosters high integrity and collaboration, empowering you to excel. Dotmatics is a company built by scientists, for scientists. Combined, we are now the world’s largest cloud-based scientific research R&D platform. We need your help to keep growing and pioneering the future.

We are Science Driven. We are Customer Centric. We are Better Together.

What do we need

As a Validation Engineer, you will execute and contribute to validation activities for the Dotmatics Luma platform and its internal systems operating under GxP requirements. As a key contributor to computer system validation (CSV) and computer software assurance (CSA), you will help ensure that software development, testing, and release activities comply with applicable regulations and standards, including 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, GAMP 5, FDA CSA guidance, ICH Q10, and ISO 9001 as applicable.

You will also take ownership of our in-house validation application. This tool manages requirements, risk assessments, traceability, test evidence, and validation report generation for each Luma release. You will keep it current as our processes, products, and regulatory expectations change. You don't need to be a software developer on day one: we will provide training and mentoring on the tool's codebase and the AI-assisted development tools we use to maintain it.

The Validation Engineer partners closely with Product, Engineering, DevOps, and Quality Management teams to apply validation best practices throughout the software development lifecycle (SDLC), ensuring traceable, audit-ready deliverables that meet customer and regulatory expectations.

In this role you will get to:

  • Author and review validation lifecycle documentation, including Validation Master Plans, URS, FRS, Traceability Matrix, Risk Assessments, and IQ, OQ, and PQ protocols and reports. You will follow GAMP 5 principles, including risk-based approaches to validation, with guidance from senior validation and quality colleagues.
  • Gather, document, and manage product requirements (URS/FRS) with Product and Engineering. You will maintain them in tools such as Jira and Confluence and make sure they are clear, testable, and traceable to test evidence.
  • Work with the software quality team and DevOps to develop, review, and run IQ, OQ, and PQ protocols using automated tools such as Cypress.
  • Own and maintain the internal validation application. This includes:
    • Configuring and updating requirement, risk, traceability, and report templates.
    • Adjusting the tool's workflows and integrations (Jira, Zephyr, Confluence, automated test results) as our processes change.
    • Making changes to the tool under appropriate change control.
  • Make improvements and fixes to the validation tool's codebase (Python/Flask web application) with support from Engineering. You will use AI coding assistants (e.g., Cursor, Claude) to plan, implement, test, and document changes, and you will follow our code review and deployment process (Git, GitHub Actions).
  • Maintain and refine the AI features within the validation tool, such as AI-assisted requirement drafting. This includes reviewing prompt quality and output accuracy, and making sure use stays within company AI governance and data protection policies.
  • Use AI tools (e.g., generative AI assistants) to draft, review, and quality-check validation documentation, test scripts, and traceability, always applying human review and following company AI governance and data protection policies.
  • Apply the GAMP 5 framework to help determine appropriate validation strategies and documentation requirements, including the assurance approach for the validation tool itself.
  • Keep the validation tool's user and technical documentation up to date, and train colleagues on how to use it.
  • Support and share knowledge with junior validation team members and QA staff on validation methodologies and documentation best practices.
  • Serve as a go-to resource within Luma for GAMP 5, 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, and applicable ISO standards.
  • Provide validation guidance and training to engineers, QA analysts, and project managers on CSV/CSA principles, IQ/OQ/PQ expectations, and 21 CFR Part 11 controls.

We are looking for people who can support customer-facing validation activities, coordinate validation testing and defect resolution, assist with CAPA investigations and audit responses, and collaborate with the Quality Management team to maintain document control, periodic reviews, and overall audit readiness for validation artefacts.

The key skills we are looking for:

  • Solid working knowledge of GAMP 5, 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, and GxP requirements as they apply to software systems.
  • Approximately 5 years' experience in computer system validation, software quality assurance, or a related role, ideally within a GxP-regulated environment.
  • Familiarity with ISO 9001 quality management system principles.
  • Demonstrated experience authoring and executing IQ/OQ/PQ protocols, traceability matrices, and validation summary reports, including using automated testing tools (e.g., Cypress, Playwright) to generate and capture test evidence.
  • Understanding of the software development lifecycle (SDLC) and Agile methodologies.
  • Hands-on experience using AI tools (e.g., generative AI assistants) to improve productivity in documentation, test design, or analysis. You should understand responsible use, data confidentiality, and the need for human review of AI outputs.
  • Product management skills to support requirements management, including eliciting and writing clear, testable requirements and user stories, refining and prioritizing backlogs, and working with stakeholders in Jira, Confluence, or similar tools.
  • Experience validating cloud-based systems, SaaS applications, or commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software.
  • A technical mindset and a willingness to learn to maintain and extend a software tool. You should be comfortable picking up new technical skills with training. Some exposure to scripting or programming (e.g., Python, SQL) is helpful but not required.

You may also have:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Biology, Chemistry, Engineering, or a related field (preferred but not required).
  • Background in regulated life sciences environments, such as pharmaceutical, biotech, or medical device industries.
  • Experience with Python, web applications (e.g., Flask), Git/GitHub, or CI/CD pipelines.
  • Experience using AI coding assistants (e.g., Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code) to build or modify software.
  • Familiarity with Gherkin/BDD test specifications, Zephyr, or the Jira/Confluence APIs.
  • Exposure to Databricks, AWS, or other cloud platforms.
  • Experience qualifying or validating in-house tools used in a regulated quality system.

Research shows us the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting outstanding candidates, so please don’t hesitate to apply — we’d love to hear from you.

By submitting your application, you agree that Dotmatics may collect your personal data for recruiting, global organization planning, and related purposes. Dotmatics Privacy Notice explains what personal information we may process, where we may process your personal information, our purposes for processing your personal information, and the rights you can exercise over Dotmatics use of your personal information.

Dotmatics is an equal opportunity employer. We are a welcoming place for everyone, and we do our best to make sure all people feel supported and connected at work.

title: Cocoa Sustainability Data & Reporting (London, All locations, GB)
description:
About The Hershey Company

The Hershey Company (NYSE: HSY) is an industry-leading snacks company known for making more moments of goodness through its iconic brands. With a strong portfolio across chocolate, confectionery, and salty snacks, Hershey delights consumers every day.
At Hershey, we are committed to creating sustainable value for farmers, communities, and consumers. Through our Cocoa For Good strategy, we invest in programs that improve farmer livelihoods, protect children, empower communities, and preserve ecosystems across cocoa-growing regions worldwide.

How will you fit in the big picture?

As a member of the Cocoa Sustainability team, the Manager, Cocoa Data & Reporting will play a critical role in advancing Hershey's sustainability strategy through the effective management, analysis, and reporting of complex cocoa sustainability data.
This position serves as a bridge between sustainability, procurement, reporting, and digital transformation initiatives, helping ensure the integrity, accuracy, and transparency of data that supports Hershey's Cocoa For Good commitments. Working closely with regional teams, suppliers, implementing partners, and cross-functional stakeholders, the role will strengthen reporting capabilities, improve data governance, enhance traceability systems, and support compliance with evolving sustainability regulations and disclosure requirements.
The successful candidate will combine strong analytical capabilities with business acumen to transform large, complex datasets into actionable insights that support strategic decision-making and continuous improvement across Hershey's cocoa supply chain.

What will you do?

Digital Transformation & Data Management

  • Lead and manage cocoa sustainability data workstreams, ensuring accurate execution of reporting processes, compliance with applicable controls, and proactive stakeholder engagement.
  • Manage relationships with data providers, suppliers, and implementing partners to ensure data quality, completeness, consistency, and timely reporting.
  • Analyze large-scale sustainability datasets comprising more than five million data points annually and develop solutions that increase the value and usability of available data.
  • Identify opportunities for automation, process standardization, and digital transformation to improve operational efficiency and reporting accuracy.
  • Perform root cause analyses of reporting and data-quality issues and implement corrective and preventive actions.
  • Support the development of new tools and systems that strengthen documentary and physical traceability across cocoa supply chains.
  • Partner with internal teams to design and maintain dashboards, scorecards, visualizations, and reporting solutions that enable data-driven decisions.
  • Collaborate with enterprise-wide digital and ESG initiatives, ensuring cocoa sustainability requirements are integrated into broader business programs.
  • Conduct market and technology research to identify emerging data solutions, sustainability methodologies, and strategic opportunities.

Sustainability Reporting & Disclosures

  • Lead coordinated reporting activities supporting internal and external sustainability disclosures.
  • Manage qualitative and quantitative contributions to ESG reporting, industry reporting requirements, and sustainability-related stakeholder requests.
  • Partner with regional teams and implementation partners to improve reporting consistency and accountability across cocoa-origin countries.
  • Support the collection, validation, and reporting of sustainability metrics, including traceability, GIS, environmental, and greenhouse gas-related data.
  • Maintain disclosure control procedures and improve the audit readiness and assurance of sustainability information.
  • Establish and maintain evidence standards, documentation requirements, and quality controls for sustainability communications and published materials.
  • Develop executive-level reporting materials that communicate strategic insights, program performance, and key sustainability outcomes.

Strategy, Innovation & Continuous Improvement

  • Support the execution of Hershey's cocoa data and sustainability roadmap through the management of assigned strategic projects.
  • Identify opportunities to leverage emerging technologies, analytics, and digital tools to advance cocoa sustainability objectives.
  • Build organizational capability by promoting data-driven decision-making and supporting adoption of new systems and processes.
  • Participate in cross-functional initiatives and external working groups as a subject matter expert representing Hershey's sustainability interests.
  • Generate insights and recommendations that support performance management, value measurement, compliance requirements, and long-term strategic planning.

Minimum Education & Requirements

3+ years

title: DevOps Tech Lead
description:
At R3, we are building the on-ramp for the next trillion dollars of assets to move on-chain, bridging the worlds of traditional finance (TradFi) and decentralized finance (DeFi). We are launching institutional-grade RWA yield vaults, fully composable and integrated into Solana DeFi.

About the role

We're looking for a DevOps Tech Lead to own the infrastructure, reliability, and deployment practices behind our Solana-based protocol. You'll be the technical authority on how our on-chain programs and supporting off-chain services are built, deployed, monitored, and kept running at the reliability our users and partners expect. This is a hands-on technical leadership role: you'll set direction on tooling and architecture, lead incident response, and raise the bar on operational maturity across the team, while still writing infrastructure code and debugging production issues yourself.

Depending on candidate strengths and team needs, this role can include line management of a small DevOps/SRE team and/or a strong SRE remit (SLOs, on-call, chaos/incident engineering).

What you'll do

  • Lead the DevOps strategy for the protocol: infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD for on-chain programs and off-chain services, secrets and key management, and release processes for program upgrades.
  • Build and maintain observability across the stack incl. metrics, logs, tracing, and alerting for on-chain programs, oracles/relayers, and off-chain services, and drive down mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-resolve.
  • Act as technical lead for infrastructure incidents: define runbooks, lead on-call rotations, run postmortems, and track remediation to closure.
  • Harden operational security: upgrade authority controls, multisig/governance processes for program deployments, and infrastructure access controls.
  • Partner closely with protocol engineers to understand upcoming program changes, compute/account constraints, and how they affect infrastructure capacity and deployment risk.
  • Manage relationships with third-party RPC providers and cloud/infra vendors; make build-vs-buy calls on infrastructure tooling.
  • Define and track SLOs/SLIs for RPC latency and transaction landing rates against our current (third-party) RPC infrastructure; report on reliability to engineering leadership.
  • Mentor engineers on Solana-specific operational practices (program deployment/upgrade flows, compute/account constraints, RPC behaviour and rate limits).
  • (If managing) Line-manage a small team of DevOps/SRE engineers: hiring, performance, growth planning, and day-to-day technical direction.

Key requirements: must haves:

  • Significant hands-on Solana experience: program deployment/upgrade workflows, working with the Agave/Solana CLI, RPC methods, and debugging on-chain program or transaction issues in production.
  • Strong DevOps fundamentals: infrastructure-as-code (Terraform/Pulumi), containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes), and CI/CD pipeline design (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or similar).
  • Experience with monitoring and observability stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, Loki/ELK, PagerDuty or similar).
  • Comfortable with Linux systems administration, networking, and cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP/Azure).
  • Experience leading incident response and driving postmortem/root-cause processes.
  • Strong scripting/automation ability (Bash, Python, or Go) for operational tooling.
  • Clear communicator who can work directly with protocol engineers, security, and leadership.

Key requirements: nice to haves:

  • 7-12 years of hands on experience in DevOps practices
  • Experience leading a team of DevOps engineers
  • Experience with other blockchain infrastructure (EVM chains, Cosmos SDK, or similar) for comparative context.
  • Familiarity with oracle infrastructure (e.g. Chainlink, Pyth) and cross-program integrations.
  • Experience with validator economics i.e. staking, delegation, commission strategy, and jito-solana/MEV-aware operations.
  • Prior experience as an SRE: formal SLO/error-budget practice, chaos engineering, capacity planning.
